text: Which statement best explains why the sun appears to move across the sky during the day? F) Earth is closest to sun in winter G) Earth is revolving around the sun H) Earth is tilted at 23.5 degrees J) Earth is rotating on its axis
skill: earth science - Earth's rotation causes the sun's apparent daily motion

text: A student looks at a lit nightlight through two cardboard tubes, one bent and one straight. Through which tube, if any, will the light be seen and why? A) bent tube only, light bounces off sides and travels through B) straight tube only, light travels in a straight line directly to the eye C) both tubes, light travels equally well along straight and curved paths D) neither tube, both absorb all light
skill: physical science - light travels in straight lines

text: A student places objects in a bucket of water to see if they float: toothpick, plastic paper clip, penny, cork, metal spoon, vegetable oil. Which set of items is less dense than water (floats)? F) plastic paper clip, penny, cork G) toothpick, metal spoon, plastic paper clip H) metal spoon, vegetable oil, penny J) toothpick, cork, vegetable oil
skill: physical science - density and floating

text: A food chain is shown: grasses -> grasshopper -> frog -> snake -> hawk. Which role do the grasses have in the food chain? A) decompose small organisms to produce energy B) prevent the food chain from containing too many carnivores C) capture energy from the sun and are food for consumers D) break down dead organisms into simpler substances
skill: life science - producers in a food chain

text: A student sets up two identical wet sponges: one next to a fan, one under a lamp, to investigate ways to speed up evaporation. Which forms of energy are being compared in this investigation? A) light energy and electrical energy B) mechanical energy and electrical energy C) light energy and thermal energy D) mechanical energy and thermal energy
skill: physical science - forms of energy (mechanical from moving air, thermal from heat) affecting evaporation rate

text: A table shows days to sprout and days until harvest for plants: Green beans (6 days to sprout, 50-70 days to harvest), Watermelon (4-5 days, 80-100 days), Cucumber (2-5 days, 55-65 days), Pumpkin (3-4 days, 85-120 days). Which statement is supported by the data? F) Pumpkins take the most time to sprout AND to be ready for harvest G) Green bean seeds sprout faster because they are smaller H) Cucumbers are ready for harvest in less time than watermelons J) Watermelon seeds take longer to sprout because the plants produce large fruit
skill: life science - interpreting a data table about plant growth

text: Students make a solar system model on the playground, with the school building representing the sun and round objects representing each planet. Which planet should they place at the greatest distance from the school building? A) Jupiter B) Neptune C) Mercury D) Saturn
skill: space science - relative distances of planets from the sun

text: Students observe a gerbil in a cage and record: it twitches its whiskers, it burrows in the bedding, it drinks water from a metal tube, it walks on four legs. Which observation is most likely a LEARNED behavior (not instinctive)? F) twitching whiskers G) burrowing in bedding H) drinking water from a metal tube J) walking on four legs
skill: life science - distinguishing learned behavior from instinct

text: A student plans to make a chart describing each process in the water cycle. Which sentence should describe the process of CONDENSATION? A) Water flows downhill B) Liquid water turns into water vapor C) Polar ice turns into liquid water D) Water vapor collects to form droplets
skill: earth science - water cycle vocabulary (condensation)

text: Students study barracudas (a type of ocean fish) and gather observations. Which observation describes barracudas interacting with a LIVING element of their ecosystem? F) barracudas can travel quickly using surface ocean currents G) barracudas live around hard structures such as oil rigs and jetties H) barracudas are predators of other fish J) barracudas tend to live in warm waters
skill: life science - distinguishing biotic (living) from abiotic (non-living) ecosystem interactions

text: Four examples of objects using different types of energy: Example 1) wind turbines spinning, Example 2) campfire burning, Example 3) hammer hitting a nail, Example 4) wrecking ball breaking down a building. Which examples use MECHANICAL energy to perform their function? A) Examples 1, 2, and 4 B) Examples 1, 3, and 4 C) Examples 1 and 2 only D) Examples 3 and 4 only
skill: physical science - identifying mechanical energy (motion-based) vs other energy forms

text: A hawk has sharp curved talons for gripping prey; a chicken has flatter feet suited for walking and scratching the ground for food. The difference between the shapes of their feet is most likely associated with the: A) predators that hunt them B) climate in which they live C) way they get their food D) distance they can fly
skill: life science - structural adaptations related to feeding method

text: A student is classifying objects. Answering which question will provide the BEST evidence that an object is a metal? F) What is its mass? G) What is its physical state? H) Does it conduct thermal energy? J) How quickly does it dissolve in water?
skill: physical science - properties of metals (thermal conductivity)

text: Two box turtles live in a zoo habitat. Visitors observed: 1) sliding into a small pond, 2) eating a strawberry, 3) digging a hole in sandy soil, 4) climbing onto a flat rock, 5) holding an earthworm in its mouth, 6) walking across the area. Which TWO observations best describe how box turtles interact with LIVING parts of their environment? A) observations 4 and 6 B) observations 2 and 5 C) observations 1 and 5 D) observations 3 and 4
skill: life science - identifying interactions with living (biotic) parts of an environment

text: A student pours 14 grams of sugar into a jar filled with 500 milliliters of water and stirs thoroughly to make a solution. Which change most likely occurs to the sugar when added to the water? F) the sugar breaks down to form a new substance G) the sugar changes water into a new substance H) the sugar floats on the surface of the water J) the sugar completely dissolves in the solution
skill: physical science - dissolving as a physical change, not a chemical change

text: A student observes part of a plant with a microscope. Which statement describes a behavior of light in the microscope? A) light travels through the microscope lens without changing direction B) moving in straight lines causes light to increase in brightness C) light refracts (bends) through the lens of the microscope D) moving in straight lines keeps light from reflecting
skill: physical science - refraction of light through a lens

text: A student lists resources that can be used to produce electricity: Wind, Coal, Natural gas, Water power, Petroleum. Which of these resources are RENEWABLE resources? F) Wind, water power G) Wind, coal, and natural gas H) Coal, water power, and petroleum J) Coal, natural gas, water power, and petroleum
skill: earth science - renewable vs non-renewable energy resources

text: Butterflies have very long, tubelike tongues. Hummingbirds also have very long tongues. Which statement best describes why butterflies and hummingbirds both have long tongues? A) they both migrate B) they are both attracted to brightly colored flowers C) they eat the same type of food (nectar) D) they have the same predators
skill: life science - structural adaptations related to a shared food source

text: Students conduct an investigation: 1) grind 50 grams of cereal into a fine powder, 2) stir the cereal powder into 500 mL of warm water, 3) hold a magnet against the side of the beaker, 4) stir the mixture for three minutes. The students are trying to determine the presence of which substance in the cereal? A) Sugar B) Iron C) Salt D) Wheat
skill: physical science - using a magnet to test for the presence of iron

text: Characteristics of the tundra biome: long winters with temperatures near -34°C, less than 25 cm of precipitation per year, thin topsoil over frozen ground, plants include mosses, grasses, small shrubs. Based on this description, which pair of animals is LEAST likely to live in the tundra? A) caribou and arctic fox B) muskox and snowy owl C) polar bear and arctic hare D) heron and alligator
skill: life science - matching animals to biome/habitat characteristics

text: A student makes a model with objects representing the sun, Earth, and the moon for a class demonstration. Which action should the student do with the objects to demonstrate a complete DAY-NIGHT cycle of Earth? F) move the moon around Earth once G) spin the sun in a circle once H) move Earth around the sun once J) spin Earth in a circle once (on its axis)
skill: earth/space science - Earth's rotation causes day and night

text: Scientists have uncovered palm plant fossils in Alaska (a very cold, northern state). Modern-day palm plants only grow in tropical (warm) climates. This discovery suggests that this area in Alaska once was: A) covered with an ocean B) warmer than it is now C) populated by polar bears D) changed by earthquakes
skill: earth science - using fossil evidence to infer past climate

text: Which land formation is correctly paired with the force that made it? F) A canyon was formed by a river cutting through rock over time G) A sand dune was formed by an earthquake H) A river delta was formed by wind J) A layered rock formation was formed by ice
skill: earth science - matching land formations to the geological forces that created them

text: A group of students captures several insects in a park and observes them in terrariums before releasing them. Each of the following characteristics is likely an INHERITED trait EXCEPT: A) a fly's missing antenna B) a butterfly's black-and-yellow stripes C) a dragonfly's two sets of wings D) a beetle's green spots
skill: life science - distinguishing inherited traits from acquired/injury-based characteristics

text: Students want to build a desert garden and need soil that drains water away easily. They test different soils: Sand (200mL initial, 175mL drained through, 25mL remaining), Clay (200mL, 115mL through, 85mL remaining), Silt (200mL, 150mL through, 50mL remaining), Gravel (200mL, 190mL through, 10mL remaining). Based on the table, which two soil types are best for the desert garden? F) Clay and sand G) Sand and gravel H) Gravel and silt J) Silt and clay
skill: earth science - interpreting a data table about soil drainage properties

text: A student pours equal amounts of water and cooking oil into a jar, shakes it for five seconds, then lets it sit for ten minutes. After ten minutes, the oil forms a layer on top of the water. Which conclusion best compares a property of cooking oil and water? A) cooking oil is less dense than water B) water is less dense than cooking oil C) water dissolves in cooking oil D) cooking oil dissolves in water
skill: physical science - density comparison based on liquid layering

text: Large oil fields are found underground in certain regions. How did these oil fields most likely form? F) dead plants and animals were buried for millions of years G) plants were eaten by consumers that left fossilized remains H) heat caused underground rocks to undergo chemical changes J) rocks at the surface of Earth melted and then solidified
skill: earth science - formation of fossil fuels

text: Students build a balloon-rocket car: air rushes out of a balloon through a straw attached to a car, pushing the car forward. When the air is released and rushes out of the straw in one direction, which statement correctly describes the motion of the car? A) The car moves in the same direction as the escaping air B) The car moves in the opposite direction of the escaping air C) The car speeds up only because the straw becomes lighter as air is released D) The car does not move because the air simply escapes into the surroundings
skill: physical science - Newton's third law (action-reaction), demonstrated by a balloon rocket

text: Students observe three objects on a lab tray: a copper penny, iron filings, and a tin can lid. They classify the objects based on physical properties common to ALL THREE objects. Based on their common properties (all are metals, though not all are magnetic since copper isn't), how should these objects be classified? F) Insulate thermal energy, Bendable, Attract to magnets G) Soluble in water, Attract to magnets, Conduct thermal energy H) Conduct electrical energy, Bendable, Soluble in water J) Conduct thermal energy, Conduct electrical energy, Not soluble in water
skill: physical science - common properties of metals

text: A fast-growing, non-native water plant now grows in many lakes and can spread over the entire surface of a pond or lake. Which effect will most likely occur when this plant covers a lake? A) small fish will have fewer places to hide from predators B) less sunlight will reach the plants that grow underwater C) several new trees will grow along the lake shore D) deer will have to find another source of water
skill: life science - effects of invasive species on an ecosystem

text: Students conduct experiments to investigate friction. Which experiment will BEST test the effect of friction on objects? F) drop two balls from the same height at the same time G) roll two marbles on the carpet from the same starting point at the same time with the same force H) roll three marbles across three DIFFERENT surfaces from the same starting point, same time, same force J) release two balls from the top of a ramp at the same time
skill: scientific method - designing a controlled experiment to test one variable (surface/friction)
